Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end so we stay aligned: 

Recap
- Objective: Run production inference for Acme Health patient-facing features behind a private network (no public endpoints).
- Primary constraints you called out: HIPAA-compatible isolation, egress control, and minimal network changes to your existing VPCs.
- Deployment mode leaning: Private VPC deployment (Redwood Private) — you wanted clarification between PrivateLink vs VPC peering and IP allowlist options.

Open items / proposed next steps
1) Network topology preference: please confirm if Acme prefers AWS PrivateLink (endpoint services) or VPC Peering/Transit Gateway. Both are supported; pros/cons below.
2) CIDR/IP allowlist: send the IP ranges (or confirm if you want us to publish a static egress set) — we can support customer-managed allowlists or our PrivateLink setup.
3) Timeline & approvals: identify network admin(s) to approve the change and a target deploy week.
4) Technical deep dive: Dylan (SE) will follow up with a short network diagram and specific firewall rules.

Attachment: draft network_diagram (placeholder) — Dylan will attach the finalized diagram and a short install guide.

If it helps, can we do a 30-minute technical call tomorrow to walk the diagram with your network team? I put a couple of proposed times below.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Subject: Re: Private VPC follow-up: networking options (PrivateLink / VPC peering) & next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the quick responses. Short answers up front, then details and an attached diagram + setup guide.

Summary
- PrivateLink: provides ENIs in your VPC via an endpoint service and avoids route-table changes. From an access perspective you keep control entirely. For egress IPs, the traffic originates from our PrivateLink ENIs inside your VPC, so you can restrict to those ENI IPs or to the interface endpoint's private IPs.
- VPC Peering / TGW: simpler for some net teams if they already use TGW, but requires route propagation and can expose more network surface.

Recommendation
- Given your preference to avoid route changes, PrivateLink is the recommended path. We'll publish the exact endpoint instructions and the NLB/ENI IP ranges for allowlisting.

Technical details (high level)
- We offer two Private setups:
  1) Customer-facing ENI PrivateLink (recommended) — Redwood creates an endpoint service; you create an interface endpoint in your VPC. Traffic terminates on our PrivateLink; no public egress.
  2) Private peering via TGW — we can peer peering endpoints but this requires route table changes and may need additional peering approvals.
- For IP allowlists: if you want static IPs, we can front the PrivateLink with a customer-managed NLB in your account, or provide a small set of ENI private IPs for firewall rules. We'll include both options on the diagram.

Attached: redacted_network_diagram.png (high level topology), redacted_private_vpc_setup_guide.pdf (step-by-step instructions and firewall snippets).

Firewall rules (examples)
- Allow outbound to interface endpoint private IP range: 10.10.32.0/28 (example) on TCP 443
- If using customer NLB: allow traffic from NLB IPs to your application subnets on the chosen ports

Next steps
1) Please confirm you want us to proceed with PrivateLink.
2) If yes, share a preferred VPC/subnet for the interface endpoint and the network contact (Karen).
3) We'll schedule a 30-minute technical call and share a pre-call checklist.

Happy to hop on a call tomorrow 11:00–11:30am PST or Thursday afternoon.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Attachments: redacted_network_diagram.png (image), redacted_private_vpc_setup_guide.pdf (pdf)
